cards.text: We're picking right back up, friend. The LORD is speaking through Jeremiah the prophet about Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 50:1). Now He gives orders to go up against Merathaim and Pekod, and He's clear about it: "Do all that I have commanded you," declares the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD sends someone up against Merathaim and Pekod. What does He order done to them?

answers.text: Kill them and devote them to destruction
Warn them and give them a year
Capture them and bring them to Zion

cards.text: Then comes the noise of battle in the land, the noise of great destruction. And there's Babylon, the hammer of the whole earth.

cards.question: In this battle, Babylon, the hammer of the whole earth, is still swinging strong.
Broken and shattered, Babylon has become a ___ among the nations.

cards.text: Now God tells Babylon, "I laid a snare for you, O Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it." That's me and a rolling pin on the bakery floor: didn't see it, then BAM, I'm staring at the ceiling, base and all.

cards.question: God says Babylon was found and captured in His snare. Why?

answers.text: Because her walls were too low
Because her king broke a treaty

cards.text: In the land of the Chaldeans, the Lord GOD of Hosts is at work, and He has opened His armory. When folks opened MY old junk drawer, all they found was me, a twist tie and some dead batteries, so friend, this is a WHOLE different drawer.

cards.question: The LORD opens His armory against the land of the Chaldeans. What does He bring out?

cards.text: The orders keep coming: come against her from the farthest border, break open her granaries, pile her up like mounds of grain. Kill all her young bulls, and woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.

cards.question: The orders against Babylon say to leave her a few survivors.

cards.text: Then a call to listen. Fugitives and refugees are getting out of Babylon, and they're showing up in Zion.

cards.question: The refugees from Babylon reach Zion. What are they declaring there?

answers.text: The vengeance of the LORD for His temple
The kindness of the king of Babylon
A plan to rebuild Babylon's walls

cards.text: Next, every archer who strings a bow gets summoned to camp all around Babylon, so no one escapes. That's me with a fresh batch on the cooling rack: mustache wrapped around EVERY side, and not ONE cookie is leaving that tray.

cards.question: Babylon defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, so the order is to repay her according to her ___.

cards.text: So her young men will fall in the streets, and her warriors will be silenced. Then God says it straight: "Behold, I am against you, O arrogant one," declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.

cards.question: God says the arrogant one will stumble and fall. Who will pick him up?
God says He will kindle a fire in the arrogant one's cities.

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts speaks about His own people: Israel and Judah are oppressed, and their captors hold them fast, refusing to release them. Stuck where you can't get out? Friend, I did YEARS in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Israel and Judah's captors won't let them go. But who does the LORD of Hosts say is strong?

cards.text: Their Redeemer is strong, the LORD of Hosts is His name, and He will fervently plead their case. Walk into court with THAT on your side, and the other table should just pack up and go home.

cards.question: The LORD pleads their case to bring rest to the earth, but ___ to those who live in Babylon.

cards.text: Then a line rings out, over and over: a sword is against. Against the Chaldeans, against those who live in Babylon, against her officials and wise men.

cards.question: The sword against Babylon's false prophets will make them wise.
A sword is against Babylon's warriors too. What will they be filled with?

cards.text: The sword keeps going: against her horses and chariots, against the foreigners in her midst, and against her treasuries. Friend, that is a sword with a LONG to-do list, and it is checking every box.

cards.question: With a sword against Babylon's treasuries, they will be ___.

cards.text: Then a drought comes upon her waters, and they will be dried up.

cards.question: Why does drought come upon Babylon's waters?

answers.text: Her land is full of graven images
Her farmers dug too many canals
Her king refused to share water

cards.text: So desert creatures, hyenas and ostriches will move in. And no one will ever live there again, from generation to generation.

cards.question: The LORD says no one will dwell in Babylon, just like two cities God overthrew along with their neighbors. Which two?

cards.text: Then, behold, an army is coming: a great nation and many kings, stirred up from the ends of the earth. Not ONE king, friend, MANY kings, and every single one of them RSVP'd yes.

cards.question: Behold, an army is coming from the ___ against Babylon.

cards.text: They grasp the bow and spear, and their voice roars like the sea as they line up against the Daughter of Babylon. Then the king of Babylon hears the report, and friend, nobody in history has read a report like THAT and said, "Great, love that."

cards.question: The king of Babylon hears the report about the army. What happens to his hands?

cards.text: Hands hanging limp? That's me when the timer dings and the dough is STILL sitting on the counter. Then God says one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture.

cards.question: God says it will take Him a long time to chase Babylon from her land.

cards.text: So hear the plans the LORD has drawn up against Babylon: the little ones of the flock will be dragged away, and their pasture will be made desolate. Friend, when the LORD draws up the plans, there is no second draft.

cards.question: At the sound of Babylon's capture, the earth will ___.
When Babylon is captured, a cry will be heard among the nations.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set it down for now, friend. God isn't finished talking about Babylon yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD opens His armory against the land of the Chaldeans. That wording rules out the wrong answer "Shields to guard Babylon" on its own. A baker can drop it without knowing the verse, which leaves only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card packs five separate things from Jeremiah 50:26-27 into one card: come from the farthest border, break open her granaries, pile her up like mounds of grain, kill her young bulls, and the woe on them because their day has come. That is more than two beats, so the card should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card cites only Jeremiah 50:35, but it also says the line "a sword is against" rings out "over and over." That repeat happens in 50:36-37, so the card uses verses it doesn't cite.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer "Her land is full of graven images" is the only spiritual reason, and it is the only answer that sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers, "Her farmers dug too many canals" and "Her king refused to share water," are practical and modern. In a prophecy about God judging Babylon, the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Behold, an army is coming from the ___" asks the baker to fill in the exact wording of Jeremiah 50:41. Nothing on the earlier cards points to north over south or east, so the baker can only guess. This tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 50:44 ends with God's questions: "Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?" Cards 5 and 6 tell the lion and "in an instant," but neither card mentions these questions. They are the theological peak of the verse, so the baker misses an important detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
